resolved_items.resolution: C11 passes for the selected property-(c) contract. The word 'smallest' is coherent here only as conventional infimum language, not as an assertion that a positive admissible K3 attains a minimum. The source immediately renders its intended norm construction with an infimum, and it supplies no attainment theorem. More decisively, for the zero random variable every positive K3 satisfies property (c), so the infimum is 0 and there is no smallest positive admissible K3. Reading 'smallest' as literal attainment would make the printed definition false on a basic sub-exponential example. Lean's ENNReal sInf, with admissible scales restricted to nonzero finite values, correctly represents the infimal gauge and its zero boundary value without asserting attainment.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: Definition 2.7.5 says 'smallest K3' and immediately follows with an infimum formula; Proposition 2.7.1 requires K3 > 0 but contains no attainment result. In D001, admissible ENNReal scales exclude 0 and top and invoke the property-(c) predicate D005; D002 is their sInf. For X = 0, D005 holds at every positive scale, so D002 = 0 even though 0 is not admissible. This is the standard infimum boundary case rather than a mismatch or vacuity.
